research_projects.title: High-rate multiplexed four-photon entanglement
research_projects.summary: A high-rate matter–matter entanglement system built around multiplexed quantum memories.
research_projects.details: Using two 15×15 quantum memory arrays and a 2π-pulse protocol, the work achieved 546 Hz matter–matter entanglement over 20 km of fibre without active phase stabilisation. The result surpassed TPI and SPI by 75,932× and 23×, respectively. A Python/C++ simulation pipeline supported protocol optimisation and loss modelling.

research_projects.title: AI for Science · CNN–BiLSTM entanglement classification
research_projects.summary: A hybrid deep-learning architecture for sample-efficient multipartite entanglement classification.
research_projects.details: Quantum density matrices are converted into multi-channel image representations and classified with a CNN–BiLSTM network for 3–4 qubit systems. The work covered architecture co-design, the data pipeline, and benchmarking against MLP and CNN baselines.

figures.alt: CNN and BiLSTM pipeline from measurement results to entanglement classification.
figures.caption: Multi-channel representation and hybrid CNN–BiLSTM pipeline.

research_projects.title: SLM-based OAM multimode multiplexing
research_projects.summary: A combined AOD and orbital-angular-momentum approach to increase quantum memory capacity.
research_projects.details: Combined AOD-based optical-path multiplexing with OAM modes to boost quantum memory capacity by more than 10× beyond the 225-mode state of the art. Verified high efficiency and 0.5 dB bandwidth after AOD modulation, and developed Python tools for mode characterisation and crosstalk modelling.

figures.alt: AOD and OAM optical multiplexing paths producing multiple spatial modes.
figures.caption: AOD and OAM paths for multimode multiplexing.

research_projects.title: High-dimensional AOD learning enhancement and noise analysis
research_projects.summary: A learning-based framework for feedback control and noise decomposition in high-dimensional AOD systems.
research_projects.details: The framework separates correctable and irrecoverable noise, studies five-arm feedback control with Hellinger-distance gain, and analyses ESM/CSM scaling with critical thresholds N₍c₎.

figures.alt: Signal and idler AODs addressing a selected region in a quantum memory array.
figures.caption: Signal/idler AOD control over a selected memory-array region.

research_projects.title: Rare-earth solid-state quantum memory and repeater modelling
research_projects.summary: A modelling and parameterisation framework for rare-earth-doped Y₂SiO₅ quantum memories.
research_projects.details: Built full Hamiltonian models spanning free-ion, crystal-field, Zeeman, and hyperfine terms down to low-energy spin Hamiltonians. The work included ZEFOZ analysis and comparison of AFC, spin-wave storage, NLPE-DLCZ, and single-ion repeater schemes.

figures.alt: Rare-earth crystal structure, Hamiltonian terms, and energy-level diagram.
figures.caption: Crystal-field and spin-Hamiltonian modelling view.

research_projects.title: Er³⁺:YSO single-ion node · interface and nanofabrication
research_projects.summary: An optical–microwave interface for communication-band Er³⁺:YSO single-ion repeater nodes.
research_projects.details: Designed grating couplers with Lumerical FDTD/MEEP (67.1% and 57.67% simulated peak efficiency, over 60 nm bandwidth), 50 Ω CPW layouts with COMSOL RF optimisation (about 3.99 G drive field at 1 W), and GDS/EBL/SEM fabrication workflows. Measured coupling efficiency was 10.36%.

figures.alt: SEM images of fabricated photonic structures for an Er3+:YSO interface.
figures.caption: SEM views from the nanofabrication workflow.
